sources.name: Vreeman RC, Carroll AE
sources.text: "Medical myths," BMJ 2007;335:1288-1289 (22 Dec 2007): 8 glasses as 1 of 7 myths; the "popular press" line; the 1945 recommendation as quoted, offered as "one origin" that "may" explain the rule; the "last, crucial sentence" reading; Frederick Stare's "6 to 8 glasses" recommendation, quoted as made "without references"; Valtin's review as the catalogue of "complete lack of evidence"; the hyponatraemia warning.

sources.name: Valtin H
sources.text: "'Drink at least eight glasses of water a day.' Really? Is there scientific evidence for '8 x 8'?" Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 2002;283:R993-R1004: the caffeine and alcohol amendment; the search method; "No scientific studies were found in support of 8 x 8"; caffeinated drinks and beer in moderation may count; scope (healthy, sedentary adults, temperate climate); the caveat on disease, exercise, and heat; "difficult or impossible to prove a negative."

sources.name: The Physiologist (American Physiological Society)
sources.text: Marijke Vroomen Durning, "The Science of Hydration" (July 2021): attribution of the 1945 guideline to the US Food and Nutrition Board, and the "added bit of information" that "seems to have been lost over the years."

sources.name: National Academies
sources.text: News release (11 Feb 2004) on the Institute of Medicine's Dietary Reference Intakes for water: 2.7 L and 3.7 L of total water; about 80% from beverages including caffeinated ones, 20% from food; "letting thirst be their guide"; Lawrence Appel's "We don't offer any rule of thumb" quote.

sources.name: Institute of Medicine
sources.text: Dietary Reference Intakes for Water, Potassium, Sodium, Chloride, and Sulfate (released 2004, published 2005), chapter 4, "Water": the adequate intakes for ages 19 to 30 set at NHANES III median intakes; "no single daily total water requirement for a given person"; the 33.8 fl oz per litre conversion used for the ledger arithmetic (64 oz is about 1.9 L; 2.5 L is about 10.6 8-ounce glasses); Valtin 2002 in the reference list.

sources.name: NHS
sources.text: "Water, drinks and hydration" (last reviewed 17 May 2023): the Eatwell Guide's "6 to 8 cups or glasses of fluid a day"; "This is just a guide"; tea and coffee count.
